newsitem.title: UK: Clarke to stagger UK public sector pay rises-paper.
newsitem.headline: Clarke to stagger UK public sector pay rises-paper.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke is preparing to stagger pay awards for public sector workers to relieve pressure on tight budgets, the Guardian newspaper reported on Friday.

Health workers, teachers and the armed forces are expected to receive pay rises of between 3.2 and 3.4 percent, the Financial Times said on Friday but the Guardian said Clarke is likely to phase those awards in in stages, gambling that workers will be assuaged by the relatively high overall increase.
A cabinet meeting is scheduled for next week to discuss the pay round, the Guardian said.
The paper reported health services leaders have warned that footing the bill for such pay rises in one go would be crippling for the service. Staggering the awards would ease the burden.

Clarke is expected to support that argument despite the temptation to award the annual rises in full with an election due by May and the latest poll from the MORI organisation showing the opposition Labour Party revelling in a 25 point lead.
